desc:
An AI data readiness review checks whether your product lists, customer records, help articles and spreadsheets are tidy enough to use with AI. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your data and gives you a plain report that shows the problems and the order to fix them.

## What is AI data readiness?

AI data readiness is the state of your information when a tool can read it and give correct answers from it. Data is ready when it is complete, consistent, current and safe to share with the tool. It is not ready when the same product appears under three names, prices sit in different columns, or old policies are mixed with new ones.

A readiness review measures that gap before you build anything on top of it.

## Why messy data causes weak AI results

An AI tool does not know which of your two conflicting answers is the right one. It uses what you give it. If a help article says returns take place within a set window and an older article says something different, the tool may quote either one to a customer. If half your customer records have no email field, a campaign tool has nothing to work with.

Cleaning data after a tool is live is slower and more embarrassing than cleaning it first. Mistakes reach customers, staff lose trust in the tool, and the project gets blamed for a problem that was in the files all along.

## How tidy data improves the outcome

Good data improves accuracy, which improves everything that depends on it. A support assistant answers correctly because the help articles agree with each other. A product description tool writes useful copy because attributes such as size, material and colour are filled in the same way on every row. A report tool gives sensible totals because dates and currencies share one format.

The mechanism is simple: tools find patterns, and clean data has clear patterns. Fixing the biggest problems first gives you the largest improvement for the least effort, which is why we rank them in order.

## What a data readiness review checks

- Completeness: blank fields, missing images, empty descriptions and absent contact details.
- Duplicates: repeated products, customers listed twice, near-identical articles.
- Format consistency: dates, phone numbers, units, currencies and capitalisation.
- Naming: whether columns, tags and categories follow one clear pattern.
- Freshness: outdated prices, discontinued items and expired policies.
- Accuracy signals: entries that contradict each other.
- Structure: whether one record holds one thing, or several mixed together.
- Sensitive fields: names, addresses and other personal details that need care.
- Access: where the data lives and who can edit it.

## How we carry out the review

You send us an export of each data source, such as a spreadsheet, a product export, a list of help articles or a customer file. We read through it, run counts for gaps and duplicates, and pull out real examples of each problem so you can see them for yourself.

You then receive a report that rates each source, lists the problems from biggest to smallest and sets out cleanup steps in a sensible order. The Basic package covers a single source and its top problems. Standard covers several sources with a rating for each and advice on formats and naming. Premium goes further with a sample cleanup on a small set of rows, notes on privacy and consent, and a results call. Add-ons include an extra source, a larger cleanup and a short data rules sheet your team can follow when entering new records.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which task the data will serve before you review it.
- Fix duplicates and blanks before adding any AI tool.
- Choose one format for dates, units and names, and write it down.
- Remove or mark outdated entries instead of leaving them mixed in.
- Keep personal details out of any export you do not need to share.

**Avoid:**
- Feeding every file you own into a tool in the hope it sorts them out.
- Mixing old and new policies in the same folder.
- Cleaning by hand without a written rule, which creates new inconsistencies.
- Sharing customer exports that include more fields than the task needs.
- Treating a one-time cleanup as permanent.

## Who this is for

This review suits an online store owner who wants an AI tool to write product copy but has a catalog full of half-filled rows. It suits a service business that plans a support assistant and keeps its answers across email, a document folder and old chat messages. It also suits a manager who has been asked to prepare the company for AI and does not know where to begin.

## What we need from you

Tell us what you want to use AI for and send exports or copies of the data sources, in whatever format you have them. If personal customer details are involved, we can work from a version with names and contact fields removed. We never ask for passwords. If a source can only be viewed inside a tool, you can add us as a staff or team user with view-only access, or send screenshots and a sample.

After you order, we reply with a short checklist and confirm how each file should be sent.
